images.title: One dot plot, all measures
images.purpose: Recap the chapter on one small dot plot: minimum, maximum, range, median and mean, with an outlier pulling the mean away from the median.
images.composition: One dot plot centred on a single number line: the range bracket and median label above the dots, the scale numbers and the mean marker below the line; generous white space.
exact_structure: One horizontal grey (#6B7280) number line from 0 to 15, small ticks at every whole number, numbered under the line at 0, 5, 10 and 15 only.
Exactly 7 dots above the line: one at 3, two stacked at 4, one each at 5, 6 and 7, and one at 13. Six of them are teal (#0072B2); the single dot at 5 is reddish purple (#CC79A7).
Directly above the purple dot at 5, the label median 5.
Above all the dots, one grey (#6B7280) bracket running from 3 to 13, with range 10 at its centre, min 3 at its left end and max 13 at its right end.
Below the scale numbers, one amber (#E69F00) triangle at 6 pointing up at the line, with the label mean 6 under it.
Arithmetic check for the reviewer only, NOT drawn in the frame: 3 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 13 = 42, 42 ÷ 7 = 6; sorted 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 13, middle (4th) value 5; 13 − 3 = 10.
rejection: other than 7 dots, or other than one purple dot
median marked anywhere but 5 or mean anywhere but 6
the range bracket not running from 3 to 13
images.takeaway: A dot plot shows the spread, the median is the middle value, and the mean is the fair share, pulled up by an outlier.
images.description: A dot plot of seven values with minimum 3, maximum 13, range 10, median 5 in purple and mean 6 marked below.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask why the mean sits to the right of the median and which dot causes it.

image_decisions.why: A single annotated dot plot recaps the chapter's measures at a glance.
